entries.title: One type rule for a whole group of books, and single articles as extra content
entries.text: On the campaign page, open a group such as Adventures and set a type rule — say, only rules, items and spells — and it applies to every book in that group you put in play, unless a book sets its own choice or is exempted. An article from a compare layer can now be enabled on its own page: it is in play, its book is not, and the campaign page lists it under Extra content.

entries.title: Trades show their recipes and materials; tools and characters show what they can craft
entries.text: A new article type Trade names the tools it is practised with. Its page lists every recipe of the trade with check, time and what it yields, and the materials those recipes need, with search and a rarity filter. A tool’s page shows “Can craft”, and a character’s Craft tab lists, per tool they are proficient in, the recipes it makes — learned or not.

entries.title: Map tools in a tool bar, and fullscreen
entries.text: The map has a tool bar on the left: Select, Tokens, Measure and Fog, each with its tools above the map and a key (S, T, M, F). Fullscreen (Shift+F) gives the map the whole screen; on Play the turn planner stays with it. Boards open from a button.

entries.title: Filter by prerequisite and effect, and show what a character can use
entries.text: Feats, items and classes filter by their prerequisite (level, ability score, spellcasting, proficiency, class, ancestry) and items and feats by their effects (resistance, bonus to AC …). “Usable by” in the sidebar keeps what a character meets; what can’t be checked stays, marked “?”. The search filters the same way once one type is picked.

entries.title: Fog per character, moves the GM confirms, and reveal along moves as a campaign rule
entries.text: Rules & options › On the map: one fog for the party or one per character, players move their tokens freely outside encounters or propose moves the GM confirms on the map, and whether moves reveal the way (a map may override it). With fog per character, “For” picks whom you reveal for and whose view Player view shows.

entries.title: Books, classes and ancestries read on their own article page
entries.text: A layer’s page now shows its book right below the header — contents, search and your reading position, no separate Read tab. A class shows its level table, subclasses and features on its article page, an ancestry or background its variants and traits. Old links to the reading view and the class pages still land there. In the registry they are layout elements.

entries.title: Fog of war shows what is revealed in every browser
entries.text: With fog on, the player view and player accounts now see the revealed parts of a map in every browser — before, some browsers covered the whole map, revealed areas included.

entries.title: Help for every page
entries.text: The ? in the header opens help for the page you are on, with the What's new entries about it. On Play it explains the map tools, how fog is revealed (by hand or along moves), why there is no line of sight yet, and the turn planner with its reactions.

entries.title: Maps have their own page
entries.text: Play › Maps lists every map you can see, with a preview, sub-maps indented under their map, and filters by layer and tag. “New map” turns an uploaded or chosen map image into a map. On a session, “Map on the table” now also offers map images and makes a map from the one you pick; a map’s page says which sessions and scenes use it.

entries.title: Images show their size, their tags as badges, and become maps or tokens
entries.text: Each image in the gallery now names its resolution, aspect ratio, file size and format, and the layer it comes from. Tags stand as badges: remove one with ×, add one with “+ tag”, or tag a whole selection. “Use as…” turns an image into a map (with a grid suggested from its resolution), the token of a creature, or a prop — and links straight to the result.

entries.title: Opportunity attacks in the turn planner
entries.text: When a planned move leaves an enemy's reach, the map marks the square with ⚠ and the turn says who it provokes — Disengage first to avoid it. As the turn plays out, whoever may react is asked “Opportunity attack?”: Attack rolls into the log and uses the reaction until that creature's next turn. During an encounter, player tokens move only through the turn plan.

entries.title: Quick view of a statblock shows its key numbers
entries.text: Clicking a statblock or a creature — in the compendium preview, a popup, on a board or a map token — now shows AC, HP, speed, initiative, passive Perception and CR as one row of tiles; a character adds its current HP and conditions. The full statblock as in the book stays on the article page.

entries.title: A campaign shows the rules it plays by
entries.text: Open a campaign and switch to “Rules & options”: inventory, crafting, ability scores, starting equipment, feats, languages, travel and units, grouped, each with a sentence on what it does and the variant in use. Each variant links the rule article that explains it; where none exists yet, the GM can write one with a click.

entries.title: Only the layers in play are shown
entries.text: Lists, search, articles and their versions now name only the layers your campaign puts in play (and its compare layers). Layers that are off no longer appear as articles, filters or sources; a single line says how many articles are hidden and links to the campaign, where layers are turned on and off.

entries.title: Hit points in the character builder, and Edit opens the builder
entries.text: The builder now has a Hit points step: roll each hit die or take its average, as the campaign allows, and see the maximum with your CON. Edit on a character opens the same builder with every choice in place, so you can change a pick and see what follows — Full edit switches to all fields. Cover name, alignment, size and appearance are asked at the end.

entries.title: One layer filter, and selections you can save
entries.text: World, Story, Rules and the Compendium now follow the layers in play for the campaign — “Change layers” in the sidebar opens the campaign popup at the top. There, under “Saved selections”, save what is in play under a name, for this campaign or any, open it to see its layers, and load it again with one click.

entries.title: Edit shows only the fields that matter
entries.text: Editing or creating an article now shows the required fields and those with a value. Every other field is under “+ Add field”: search it, read what each field means, and pick one to fill it in.

entries.title: Plan your turn on the map (prototype)
entries.text: Under Play, a bar below the map shows your action, bonus action, reaction and movement, and your character's actions as tiles. Tap Move and a square, pick an attack and a target to see the chance to hit, line the steps up in order and send the turn to the GM — who confirms it, the dice are rolled into the log and your token moves.

entries.title: Layer groups switch as a whole, and Back returns to your place
entries.text: The tick on a layer group now turns every book in it on or off — no earlier selection comes back — and shows whether all, none or some of its books are in play. When you open an article from a list and go back, the page scrolls to where you were, with the same groups open.

entries.title: The character builder shows what each option brings
entries.text: Open “Effects” on an ancestry, background or class to see what it brings — a sub-ancestry includes its base — or tick “Compare” on up to four. Variants sit under their base, your pick's own choices appear right below it, and your draft is kept, so opening an article no longer loses it.

entries.title: Ancestries and backgrounds read like the class view
entries.text: Rules › Ancestries and Rules › Backgrounds list them with filters for source, size, creature type and rules version. Each page shows its traits written out and its choices with links; an ancestry lists its variants to switch between and compare, a background its tables as dice tables. The character builder links there with “More about this …”.

entries.title: Encounters have a kind
entries.text: An encounter can now say what it is: combat, social, puzzle, exploration, hazard, trap, resource or story — several at once, for a talk that turns into a fight. The kind shows in the encounter list and you can filter by it. Encounters that already had combatants are marked as combat.

entries.title: Named creatures from the books are characters
entries.text: A named creature from an imported book or adventure now stands in World as a creature of its own, with its statblock attached, in the same layer. You can give it relationships, factions and a place on the map like any character you made yourself.

entries.title: Every roll is kept in the article's log
entries.text: Dice buttons now roll on the server, and each roll is saved under Rolls on the article it was rolled on — a creature shows its statblock's rolls too, a session every roll made during it. Filter by who rolled or by session, Shift-click for advantage, Alt-click for disadvantage. The GM can roll hidden, and a campaign can show player rolls to the GM only (Player rolls visible to).

entries.title: Places from books and adventures
entries.text: Imported books and adventures now bring their places: keyed rooms, sections with their own map, and sections that describe a city, realm or building become Place articles in the book's layer, nested inside each other, linked to their scenes and maps. In the reading view a section shows the place it describes, one click away.

entries.title: Filter lists by everything a type has
entries.text: Pick a type in the compendium or an area and the sidebar offers a filter for each of its fields and connections: spells by level, school, components, concentration, ritual, saving throw, damage type and the class that grants them; items by type, rarity, attunement, price and more. The choice stays in the address, so you can share it or save it as a filter group.

entries.title: See and choose where your articles go
entries.text: Under the campaign name in the top bar you now see which layer you write to. Open it to pick another of your layers in play; the choice is saved for your account, on every device. New article and quick create start there and let you change it for one article, and editing an article in another layer says so before you save.

entries.title: Pick your write layer, empty a layer in one go
entries.text: Under Account › Layers, "Make default" picks the layer new articles go to, for example a test layer of your own. "Empty…" on a layer you own shows how many articles are in it, deletes them with their parts and the links pointing at them, and offers Undo right away.

entries.title: See at a glance where versions differ
entries.text: An article with other versions now shows a badge under its name ("2 versions · differs in tier"), and each version in the Versions box says in one sentence what it changes, or that only the source differs. A value the other version leaves out reads "not set" instead of a blank. Compare puts both versions side by side, every field and edge, with long texts compared line by line.

entries.title: Crafting checks are circles you click
entries.text: On a crafting order, each check is a circle: click once for a success, twice for a failure, three times to clear it. A failure applies the campaign rule at once and clicking back undoes it; nothing is used up until you finish. The rules themselves now live on the campaign and are shown on every recipe and order.

entries.title: Clearer choices in the character creator
entries.text: Each choice now says where it comes from ("Fighter · Skill proficiencies (choose 2)"), items in an option are links you can open in place, and "two martial weapons of your choice" or "an artisan's tools" lets you pick the actual items, which then land in the inventory.

entries.title: Read a book right at its layer
entries.text: Every layer now has a Read tab with the reading view, also before the layer is turned on, so you can look a book over first. A group shows its books as a shelf, books without text appear greyed out, and the contents fold open chapter by chapter and follow along as you read.

entries.title: Loot lies in front of you until you stow it
entries.text: What a character buys, loots or is given first lies in a "Not stowed" area above the inventory grid: drag it into the grid (with mouse or finger), tap a cell, or press Stow. The campaign decides how long it may lie there; whatever is left at the end of the session (or when the table moves on) stays behind at the session, where anyone can pick it up again.

entries.title: Your own layer as a player
entries.text: As a player, you get your own layer in each campaign you join: your character, notes and everything you create land there, just under the campaign layer. The account page marks it as your default; when a player leaves, the GM can take over what is in it.

entries.title: What's new starts with your account
entries.text: What's new now lists only what changed since your account was created, so a new player is not handed the whole history. Admins can still show everything.

entries.title: Large images show they are loading
entries.text: Maps and full-size article images show a spinning circle until the picture has arrived, instead of an empty frame that looks broken.

entries.title: Easier to read
entries.text: Long single texts such as "On arrival" or "Goal" read like prose, sortable values stay in the edit form, same-named links on a board say what they are, and a book without imported text says so when you open it to read.

entries.title: What's new
entries.text: This page: what changed on the site, newest first, with a link to the place. A dot next to "What's new" in the header says there is something you have not seen yet — on any device you sign in with.

entries.title: Campaign and layers in the header
entries.text: Under the brand, the header shows the running campaign and how many layers are in play. A click opens a popup to switch layers and groups on or off and to compare them.

entries.title: Every item given is its own copy
entries.text: Whatever a character receives — bought, looted, crafted, starting equipment, or given with "Add an item" on the inventory — is a copy of the item article: change one without touching the rest, while fixes to the article still reach every copy.

entries.title: Board areas
entries.text: A board can be split into named areas that fold away and show up as tabs along the top. They work by touch on phones and tablets too.

entries.title: Filter groups
entries.text: Save a filter as a group on a page and reach it as a sub-tab or from the ▾ next to the page in the header. The GM keeps the campaign's groups, everyone their own; a group can be the page's default.

entries.title: Search from anywhere
entries.text: Press Ctrl+K or / on any page: results appear while you type, closest first, and can be narrowed by type, layer, publisher and area. The "+" on a result shows more of it.

entries.title: Crafting at the recipe
entries.text: Start a crafting order from a recipe: its material stays reserved in the inventory of the character or party until the order is done. How crafting works is set per campaign.

entries.title: Shops: buy and sell
entries.text: A shop lists its goods with quantities, discounts and derived prices. Characters buy and sell there; what they buy becomes their own copy of the item.

entries.title: Inventory
entries.text: Characters, parties and containers carry an inventory: a grid where items can be rotated, zones that say how fast you reach something, weight or slots as the campaign decides, coins, and moving items between them.

entries.title: Transfer between installations
entries.text: The workbench moves articles and registry rows between two installations with a preview, a list of conflicts and an undo.

entries.title: Create from a selection
entries.text: When the article you want to pick in a field does not exist yet, create it right there in a small popup — it is filled in at once.

entries.title: Creature and statblock
entries.text: A creature page shows its statblock. Without one it offers "Create" or "From a template" in its place.

entries.title: Images
entries.text: Upload images and attach them to articles; they show in lists, cards and on the article page. The gallery filters by class, tag, layer and "unused", and an image's source can be replaced.

entries.title: Maps in Play
entries.text: Play › Map shows the session's map with grid, measuring, markers and sub-maps to zoom into. Fog of war, a player view, a turn indicator and token images came along.

entries.title: Live updates
entries.text: Open articles follow changes made elsewhere without reloading. The dot in the header shows whether this device is listening.

entries.title: Views in the registry
entries.text: Define your own views in the registry and adjust each one per article type. Every article type can now print the way a book page looks, and there is a handout view.

entries.title: Print an article
entries.text: "Print" on an article opens it on a single A4 sheet.

entries.title: Edges explained
entries.text: The registry says what each kind of connection between articles means and what it does.

entries.title: Layers by publisher
entries.text: Layers are grouped by publisher and category. A layer's publisher is shown on its page and can be changed there.

entries.title: Activate part of a layer
entries.text: A layer can be switched on for some areas or article types only.

entries.title: Your own layers
entries.text: Every account can create its own layer. GMs write the campaign's layer; editing something you cannot write saves your version in a layer of yours.

entries.title: Versions at every field
entries.text: Where another version of an article says something different, its value stands next to the field, marked with its layer. Which layers are compared is up to you.

entries.title: Reveal to players and the party
entries.text: "Revealed to" and "Hidden from" offer players and the party. Every campaign has its party, and characters join it when a player gets them.

entries.title: Starting equipment
entries.text: Character creation hands out starting equipment the way the campaign's rule says.

entries.title: Character creation and level up
entries.text: A step-by-step assistant builds a character from the class, ancestry and background articles: standard array, languages, choices, and the same assistant again for each level up.

entries.title: Take chapters into your story
entries.text: Chapters, scenes and single text parts of an adventure can be taken into your own story — as your version, or used as they are.

entries.title: Item effects
entries.text: Items carry effects that are calculated when an article is read, not typed in by hand.

entries.title: Quick view everywhere
entries.text: Click any named article to see its card in a popup; "Open article" takes you there. Breadcrumbs show where you are.

entries.title: Reading view
entries.text: Read a layer like a book, with a table of contents, search inside it and your reading position kept per account.

entries.title: View as a member
entries.text: The GM can look at the campaign through a member's eyes, read only, from the campaign page.

entries.title: Safe saving
entries.text: When two people change the same article, the second save merges instead of silently overwriting the first.

entries.title: Export your campaign
entries.text: "Export campaign" saves the campaign as a file.

entries.title: Link fields as a selection
entries.text: Fields that point to another article offer only articles of the right type, show them as chips and link to them by name.

entries.title: Players create articles
entries.text: Players of the campaign create and edit their own articles. Only the GM marks an article "ready", and players see what is ready — plus their own characters in any state.

entries.title: Workbench
entries.text: Checks over all articles and bulk changes with a preview and an undo, for GMs and admins. API tokens are created and revoked there too.

entries.title: Boards
entries.text: Every story article can have a board: a canvas with cards for the articles placed on it.

entries.title: Edit the registry
entries.text: Create and change article types, edges, lists and views in the registry. What a change would touch is counted first.

entries.title: Classes
entries.text: Each class shows its table, its features per level, and its subclasses side by side.

entries.title: Campaign members
entries.text: The campaign page manages members, their roles and invitations.

entries.title: Articles like a book
entries.text: The new site: header with the areas, a compendium with filters in the sidebar, "New article", and articles laid out like a book page — statblocks, spells and items included, on the phone as well.
